Store Pickup pod
Store Pickup · Meesho · pre-read for peers

Answer first, call later

14% of buyers who call a pickup store call at night, between 10 PM and 6 AM. Now, when the store is closed, tapping Call Store says so, tells you when you can call and answers the usual questions instead of dialling.

01 — Why now

A night call cost us the order, and the buyer

LOD with a buyer who called the store at 11:55 PM.

“Meesho to mereko kabhi bhi order place karne ka option de deta. Mein store pickup ka option dekha and wahan call ka option tha. Mujhe pata karna tha ki store se ghar ka distance kya hai isliye call kiya tha. But store ne 4 baate aage se sunai ki yeh kya time hai call karne ka. Iss wajah se order place nhi kiya aur aage bhi nhi karungi. Aapko clearly batana chahiye ki calling ka bhi time hai on the app, agar aisa tha toh. Mera bhaut hi bura experience raha toh order nhi kiya.”
— Buyer, LOD · called at 11:55 PM

In English: Meesho lets me place an order any time. I saw the store pickup option and there was a call option. I wanted to know the distance from the store to my home, so I called. But the store scolded me: what time is this to call? So I didn’t place the order, and I won’t in future. The app should clearly say there’s a time for calling, if there is one. It was a really bad experience, so I didn’t order.

Adoption · LOD

A night call can cost the order

Scolded for calling late, she didn’t place the order and says she won’t use it again.

Expectation

The app is open, the shop isn’t

Meesho takes orders any time and nothing tells buyers the store has calling hours. Shopkeepers get those calls at home, after closing.

Questions

They ask what the app already knows

Before ordering they ask how far the store is, whether it comes home, whether it’s safe and how long it waits. Each one is among the six answers in the sheet.

02 — Problem

14% of buyers who call a store call at night

At checkout, a buyer can pick a partner kirana store within about 400 m instead of home delivery. It’s live in limited pincodes, under 1,000 orders a day, shown to prepaid-leaning users. Pickup is prepaid/UPI only. The order waits at the store for 3 days after it arrives, and the buyer collects it in store hours by showing an OTP from the app.

The store card on the review page has a Call Store button with the shopkeeper’s number. 14% of the buyers who use it call at night, between 10 PM and 6 AM. It hurts both sides: the shopkeeper is disturbed after hours, and a buyer who gets turned away may not order at all.

Night calls ring a shopkeeper at home for questions the app could answer.

9,340 of 65,746 calling users called between 10 PM and 6 AM · TODO: date range

04 — The bet

Stop the night call at the tap, answer the question instead

Primary metricShare of calling users who call at night (10 PM–6 AM): 14% → 0%

If the app says the store is closed, when you can call and answers the usual questions, buyers don’t ring at night and don’t get turned away.

Scope: in-app, pre-order moments only
05 — Design

When the store is closed, the sheet says so and doesn’t dial

The prototype: tap Call Store on Review Your Order at night, the sheet opens instead of dialling, and the store icon closes its doors.

Rules the sheet follows

Time

The store’s own hours

The opening time comes from the store. “Tomorrow” shows only between closing and midnight; after midnight it drops.

Buttons

Never a disabled Call button

Keep it enabled and explain on tap.

Voice

You, and the shopkeeper

The app speaks to “you”. The shopkeeper is always third person.

Layout

One line, same height

Six one-line answers. Every row is the same height and nothing truncates.

Six answers to the questions people call about

Each row is a question, a one-line answer and a second line. Values in braces come from the order and store.

#QuestionAnswer
1Will my parcel wait for me?Yes, for 3 days after deliveryCollect any day, {store hours}
2Is my parcel safe there?Yes, it stays sealedHanded only to you, with your OTP
3Will it be delivered home?No, pick it up from the storeWant it home? Pick Deliver to Home
4Where’s the store?{n} min walk awayDirections on the map (See Map button)
5When will it reach the store?By {date}You’ll get an SMS when it’s ready
6Who do I share the OTP with?Only the shopkeeper, at the counterNever share it on a call
06 — Explorations

Four ways to say “closed”

Each closed style was built in all five content variants. A ends on Okay, like the default; in B and C, Call Store stays enabled and a tap explains instead of dialling.

Centred + Okay

Default

The status is the hero and its store icon closes its doors on a loop. While closed the only action is Okay, which closes the sheet. Why it won: it’s focused on telling you the store is closed, without any distraction. The video and illustration variants help general comprehension, but not in this moment; a video here would be over-solving it.

A · Dark band

Alternative

The status replaces the title as a dark band. Why it lost: it looks visually off, and it gives very little space to the one thing users need to catch right away.

More explorationsB · Strip and C · Card

B · Strip

Alternative

A slim dark notice above the daytime sheet. Why it lost: it looks visually off, and it gives very little space to the one thing users need to catch right away.

C · Card

Alternative

A dark card first in the list that hands over to the answers. Why it lost: it looks visually off, and it gives very little space to the one thing users need to catch right away.

07 — States

The status follows the clock and the store

The store icon closes its doors, then loops

The Visual Library Shop with its door split into two leaves that slide shut over a lit doorway; the light goes out and the store dims. 3.2s loop. Reduced motion: the doors stay shut.

10 — Next: open hours

The same answers in store hours, then a Call Store that dials

An idea to experiment with, not part of the night design. The sheet also opens while the store is open: answers first, then “Still have questions?” and Call Store, which dials the shopkeeper. If the answers cover the question, the call doesn’t happen. The content variant is set by the Home feed card the shopper came from.
